title: Every hair on your head could hold 10 tonnes. That is 1.67 elephants

beats.say: What if every hair on your head pulled at once? Together they could hold 10 tonnes.
beats.speak: What if every hair on your head pulled at once? Together they could hold ten tonnes.

head: WHY
10 TONNES?
beats.say: One hair can hold up to 100 grams. An average head has about 100,000 hairs. 100,000 times 100 grams is 10,000 kilograms.
beats.speak: One hair can hold up to one hundred grams. An average head has about one hundred thousand hairs. One hundred thousand times one hundred grams is ten thousand kilograms.

head: START WITH
ONE HAIR.
beats.say: Start with one single hair. It can lift a 100 gram chocolate bar off the table.
beats.speak: Start with one single hair. It can lift a one hundred gram chocolate bar off the table.

head: NOW
10 HAIRS.
beats.say: 10 hairs together hold a 1 kilogram bag of sugar.
beats.speak: Ten hairs together hold a one kilogram bag of sugar.

head: 700 HAIRS:
A WHOLE PERSON.
beats.say: Just 700 hairs could hold a 70 kilogram adult. Under 1% of your head.
beats.speak: Just seven hundred hairs could hold a seventy kilogram adult. Under one percent of your head.

head: 60,000 HAIRS:
AN ELEPHANT.
beats.say: 60,000 hairs hold an average bull savanna elephant. That is 6,000 kilograms.
beats.speak: Sixty thousand hairs hold an average bull savanna elephant. That is six thousand kilograms.

head: ALL 100,000
AT ONCE.
beats.say: Use every hair and you hold 10,000 kilograms. That is 1.67 bull elephants, hanging from one head.
beats.speak: Use every hair and you hold ten thousand kilograms. That is one point six seven bull elephants, hanging from one head.

head: NOW A
THICK HEAD OF HAIR.
beats.say: Some scalps have 150,000 hairs. That is 15,000 kilograms, 2.5 elephants.
beats.speak: Some scalps have one hundred and fifty thousand hairs. That is fifteen thousand kilograms, two point five elephants.

head: REALITY
CHECK.
beats.say: The real record: in 2014 Asha Rani pulled a London double decker bus with her hair. 12,216 kilograms, rolling on its wheels, not lifted.
beats.speak: The real record: in two thousand fourteen Asha Rani pulled a London double decker bus with her hair. Twelve thousand two hundred and sixteen kilograms, rolling on its wheels, not lifted.

beats.say: Follow Ship With Pip for more.

caption: One human hair can hold up to 100 g, and an average head has about 100,000 hairs. If every hair pulled at once, that is 10,000 kg: 1.67 average bull savanna elephants (6,000 kg each). 10 hairs hold a 1 kg bag, 700 hold a 70 kg adult, 60,000 hold one elephant. A thick head of 150,000 hairs gets to 15,000 kg, 2.5 elephants. The real record: in 2014 Asha Rani pulled a 12,216 kg London double decker bus with her hair, rolling on its wheels.
notes: Science Buddies hair strength activity (reprinted by Scientific American): a single hair 'can carry a weight of up to 100 grams' and 'an average person's head has about 100,000 hairs'. NYU Langone: 'A typical scalp bears some 100,000 to 150,000 hairs' (150,000 used as the thick head). San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance Library fact sheet: savanna elephant male 6,000 kg on average. Guinness World Records, heaviest vehicle pulled by hair (female): Asha Rani (India), 12,216 kg, a London double decker bus, 7 July 2014, Milan. The 100 g bar and 1 kg bag are defined by their labels. 70 kg is a chosen example adult mass (constant), not a sourced average. The what-if assumes every hair carries its full 100 g at once, which real hair does not do. Under 1% of your head: 700 / 100,000 = 0.7%. Strands drawn are a few dozen lines standing for the stated count; elephants drawn smaller than scale; a fractional elephant is drawn cut off at that fraction.
